delivery_phases.title: Backend Setup and Basic Routes
delivery_phases.spec_focus: Create FastAPI app, serve static frontend, implement GET / route and basic static file handling.

delivery_phases.title: Backend High Score API
delivery_phases.spec_focus: Add POST /score and GET /score endpoints with in‑memory high‑score storage, validation, and update logic.

delivery_phases.title: Frontend Static Assets and Initial Game Loop
delivery_phases.spec_focus: Build HTML canvas page, load CSS and core JS modules, implement input handling and a minimal requestAnimationFrame loop.

delivery_phases.title: Full Game Implementation and End‑to‑End
delivery_phases.spec_focus: Complete gameplay logic: ship movement, firing, enemy spawning, humanoid abduction/rescue, scoring, HUD, wave progression, and game‑over flow.

validation.spec_summary: The Defender Clone project delivers a browser‑based arcade shooter using a Python FastAPI backend and a vanilla‑JavaScript frontend. All source files live under the `defender/` directory. The backend serves static files, implements a minimal in‑memory high‑score API, and is launched with `uvicorn`. The frontend provides a fullscreen HTML5 canvas, CSS styling, and a collection of JavaScript modules that implement input handling, player ship behavior, bullet management, enemy spawning, humanoid logic, world scrolling, HUD rendering, and the main game loop with finite‑state screens (title, game, wave intro, death, game‑over). Unit tests for the backend are written with pytest and FastAPI's TestClient, covering static route serving, score posting, score retrieval, and high‑score updating rules. The full test suite can be executed from `defender/backend` via `pytest -q`. The README explains installation (`pip install -r backend/requirements.txt`), how to start the server, and the keyboard controls. The delivery is split into four phases: backend setup, backend score API, frontend scaffolding, and final complete game implementation, each with its own verification command. The final deliverable is a runnable game that can be accessed in a browser at `http://localhost:8000`, providing smooth 60 fps gameplay with neon‑styled graphics, scoring, lives, bombs, and wave progression, meeting all functional requirements described in the specification.
